Ghetto of Biella

Ghetto · Biella, Italy

In 1761 there were 26 Jews. Some were authorised by the House of Savoy to carry out money lending activities and others, towards the end of the century, cloth trading businesses; over time the Morello and Vitale companies gradually gained prestige on a nationwide scale. With the Emancipation in 1848 professional opportunities for Jews increased, and unlike other small towns in which the Community tended to dwindle, the number of Jews in Biella rose to one hundred, thanks to the city’s industrial development.
